propositions.statement: p is an arbitrary prime, K is an arbitrary field with Char K=p, and λ is an integer with 0≤λ<p.

V is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂(C)-module of highest weight λ and complex dimension λ+1. Its endomorphisms x,y,h satisfy hx−xh=2x, hy−yh=−2y and xy−yx=h. The vector v∈V is nonzero and satisfies xv=0 and hv=λv.

M⊂V is an arbitrary free abelian subgroup with an integer basis which is also a complex basis of V, and M is stable under the integer enveloping subalgebra generated by all X_r=x^r/r! and Y_r=y^r/r! (r∈N). The induced x,y,h actions on V(K)=M⊗_Z K are the actions in the target.

For i=0,…,λ, the vectors e_i=y^iv/i! form a complex basis of V. They satisfy xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ−i+1)e_(i−1) for 1≤i≤λ, ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for i<λ, ye_λ=0, and he_i=(λ−2i)e_i. For every r≥0, X_r e_i=binom(λ−i+r,r)e_(i−r) if r≤i and zero otherwise; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) if i+r≤λ and zero otherwise.

For i,j∈{0,…,λ}, let E_ij be the complex linear map sending e_j to e_i and every e_k with k≠j to zero, and put c_j=binom(λ,j), A_ij=X_(λ−i)Y_λX_λY_(λ−j), and D=∏_(t=0)^λ c_t. Each A_ij preserves M, A_ij=c_jE_ij, A_ij A_kl=δ_(jk)c_j A_il, and D Id_V=Σ_(i=0)^λ(∏_(t≠i)c_t)A_ii.

propositions.statement: For every j with 0≤j≤λ the integer c_j=binom(λ,j) has nonzero image in K; for every r with 0≤r≤λ the integer r! has nonzero image in K. Hence D=∏_(j=0)^λ c_j also has nonzero image in K.

Let A_ij^K denote the operator induced by A_ij|_M on U=M⊗_Z K and define F_ij=(c_j in K)^(-1) A_ij^K for 0≤i,j≤λ. Then F_ij F_kl=δ_(jk)F_il and Σ_(i=0)^λ F_ii=Id_U. For 0≤r≤λ the induced divided powers satisfy (r! in K)X_r^K=(x^K)^r and (r! in K)Y_r^K=(y^K)^r.

argument.text: H001 gives λ≥0 and n=λ+1. Prove hy^i v=(λ−2i)y^i v for all natural i. At i=0 this is hv=λv from H002. For the induction step temporarily assume L1: hy^qv=(λ−2q)y^qv. The relation hy=yh−2y from H002 gives hy^(q+1)v=y(hy^qv)−2y^(q+1)v=(λ−2q−2)y^(q+1)v. Discharge L1 into the implication from the q-th identity to the (q+1)-st. Natural induction proves the asserted formula for every i.

produces.statement: For every natural i, hy^iv=(λ−2i)y^iv.

argument.text: Prove xy^i v=i(λ−i+1)y^(i−1)v for all i≥1. The base i=1 follows from xyv=yxv+hv=λv using H002. For a natural q temporarily assume L2: xy^(q+1)v=(q+1)(λ−q)y^qv. Using xy=yx+h and F001 at i=q+1 yields xy^(q+2)v=[(q+1)(λ−q)+λ−2(q+1)]y^(q+1)v=(q+2)(λ−q−1)y^(q+1)v. Discharge L2 and apply natural induction on q. This proves the required identity for all positive i.

produces.statement: For all natural i≥1, xy^iv=i(λ−i+1)y^(i−1)v.

argument.text: Iterating F002 gives, for every 0≤i≤λ, x^iy^iv=i!·(∏_(t=0)^(i−1)(λ−t))v. This iteration starts at the empty product for i=0; passing from i−1 to i multiplies by i(λ−i+1). All the displayed factors are positive integers when i≤λ, hence nonzero in C. Since v≠0 by H002, y^iv and e_i=y^iv/i! are nonzero. Dividing F001 by i! also gives he_i=(λ−2i)e_i for all these i.

produces.statement: For every natural i≤λ, e_i≠0 and he_i=(λ−2i)e_i.

argument.text: To show independence, temporarily assume L3: Σ_(i=0)^λ a_i e_i=0. Fix the arbitrary index j. Apply ∏_(k=0,…,λ; k≠j)(h−(λ−2k)Id_V) to this relation. The factors commute since they are polynomials in h. By F003 every term with i≠j is killed and the remaining term is a_j(∏_(k≠j)2(k−j))e_j=0. This product is nonzero over C, including the empty-product case, and e_j≠0 by F003. Thus a_j=0. As j was arbitrary every coefficient vanishes. Discharge L3 into the implication defining linear independence, and universally quantify the arbitrary coefficient family.

produces.statement: The complex family (e_i) indexed by natural i with i≤λ is linearly independent.

argument.text: Apply M001 over C to the family e indexed by Fin n, identifying its underlying indices with 0,…,λ. H002 gives finite dimension dim_C V=λ+1=n and H001 gives λ≥0, so the index cardinal is n. F004 supplies independence. M001 gives span_C{e_0,…,e_λ}=V, and together with independence this says that these vectors are a complex basis.

produces.statement: The vectors e_0,…,e_λ are a complex basis of V.

argument.text: Define z=y^(λ+1)v. F001 gives hz=(−λ−2)z. By F005 expand z in the e basis. Comparing coefficients of hz with (−λ−2)z gives for each index i≤λ a coefficient multiplied by (λ−2i)−(−λ−2)=2(λ+1−i), which is a nonzero complex integer. Every coefficient is therefore zero, and z=0. Hence y^(λ+1)v=0; all higher powers of y applied to v also vanish.

produces.statement: y^(λ+1)v=0, and y^t v=0 for every natural t≥λ+1.

argument.text: Dividing F002 by i! gives xe_i=(λ−i+1)e_(i−1) for 1≤i≤λ, while xe_0=xv=0 by H002. The definition of e gives ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for i<λ, and F006 gives ye_λ=0. The formula for h is F003. These prove every asserted generator identity, including λ=0.

produces.statement: xe_0=0; for 1≤i≤λ, xe_i=(λ−i+1)e_(i−1); for i<λ, ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1); ye_λ=0; and he_i=(λ−2i)e_i for every i≤λ.

argument.text: For all natural i≤λ and r≥0, iterate F007. If r≤i, x^r e_i=[(λ−i+r)!/(λ−i)!]e_(i−r); after division by r!, M005 with its natural arguments n=λ−i+r and k=r identifies the coefficient with binom(λ−i+r,r). If r>i, after i lowering steps in the index one reaches e_0 and the next x kills it, so X_r e_i=0. If i+r≤λ, iteration gives y^r e_i=[(i+r)!/i!]e_(i+r); dividing by r! and using M005 with n=i+r,k=r gives binom(i+r,r). If i+r>λ, iteration reaches e_λ and the next y kills it, so Y_r e_i=0. The r=0 case uses 0!=1 and zeroth powers equal to identity. The iterations follow by induction on r using the displayed one-step coefficients; factorial cancellation is valid in C. With F005 and F007, these are exactly all clauses of the required output.

argument.text: H001 allows λ to be used as a natural index. N001 supplies the complex basis e, so the linear maps E_ij exist uniquely by linear extension of the displayed values. Put P0=Y_λX_λ. N001 gives X_λ e_k=0 for k<λ and X_λ e_λ=e_0, and Y_λe_0=e_λ. Thus P0=E_(λλ). For each i≤λ, N001 gives X_(λ−i)e_λ=e_i, so X_(λ−i)P0=E_(iλ).

produces.statement: P0=E_(λλ) and for every natural i≤λ, X_(λ−i)P0=E_(iλ).

argument.text: For every j≤λ, evaluate P0 Y_(λ−j) on each e_k. If k<j, Y_(λ−j)e_k has index k+λ−j<λ and is killed by P0. If k>j it is already zero since k+λ−j>λ. If k=j, its coefficient is binom(λ,λ−j)=binom(λ,j)=c_j, and P0 fixes e_λ. The equality of the two binomial coefficients follows by complementing subsets, equivalently from their symmetric factorial quotient. Hence P0Y_(λ−j)=c_j E_(λj). Composing on the left with X_(λ−i) and using F001 gives A_ij=c_jE_ij for all i,j. Every factor in the defining product A_ij belongs to U_Z and preserves M by H003, so A_ij preserves M. No assertion that E_ij itself preserves M is needed.

produces.statement: For all i,j≤λ, A_ij=c_jE_ij and A_ij(M)⊆M.

argument.text: Evaluation on the basis gives E_ij E_kl=δ_(jk)E_il and Σ_i E_ii=Id_V. Using F002, A_ij A_kl=c_jc_lδ_(jk)E_il=δ_(jk)c_j A_il. Also (∏_(t≠i)c_t)A_ii=(∏_t c_t)E_ii=D E_ii. Sum this equality over i=0,…,λ to obtain D Id_V=Σ_i(∏_(t≠i)c_t)A_ii. All coefficients are integers, and every A map preserves M by F002. This proves the required output, with empty products equal to one when λ=0.

For every natural r with 0≤r≤λ, H001 gives r<p. Apply M004 with ring K and prime p. The factorial r! cast to K is a unit and hence nonzero: if a unit were zero, multiplying by its inverse would force 1=0 in the field K. This covers r=0 as 0!=1.

produces.statement: For every natural r≤λ, (r! in K)≠0.

argument.text: For every natural j≤λ apply M005 with n=λ and k=j to get binom(λ,j)j!(λ−j)!=λ! in the natural numbers and thus after casting to K. F001 applies to j, λ−j, and λ, since each lies between zero and λ. The right side is nonzero, so its factor (c_j in K) cannot vanish. Finally D is a finite product of these nonzero field elements and is nonzero: a finite product of nonzero elements in a field is nonzero, by induction using inverses. Together with F001 this proves the required output. At λ=0 this simply states that all displayed elements are one.

argument.text: H003 makes M a Z-module. Its admissibility implies that x=X_1,y=Y_1 and every X_r,Y_r preserve M; N002 supplies preservation for A_ij. Each restriction is Z-linear because the original map is complex-linear. Use M003 to choose ρ. Use M007 to choose τ. The flip is K-linear for the K-action specified in D008: on a pure tensor m⊗b one has τ(a·(m⊗b))=ab⊗m=a·(b⊗m)=a·τ(m⊗b). The same holds for arbitrary tensors by additivity, since tensors are finite sums of pure tensors. Its inverse is K-linear by the same formula or bijectivity.

produces.statement: The chosen flip τ is a K-linear equivalence and ρ is a unital ring homomorphism satisfying ρ(t)(a⊗m)=a⊗t(m) for every t∈End_Z(M), a∈K and m∈M. For all natural r and indices i,j≤λ, the operators x,y,X_r,Y_r,A_ij preserve M.

argument.text: Conjugate by the K-linear equivalence τ and set σ(t)=τ^(-1)ρ(t)τ. Composition and the formula ττ^(-1)=Id show directly that σ is a unital ring homomorphism. On a pure tensor, σ(T|_M)(m⊗a)=T(m)⊗a, so it is exactly T^K from D009 for every lattice-preserving T under discussion. An identity on V between integer linear combinations of compositions of such maps restricts to an identity on M, and applying σ transfers it to U. In particular the two identities of N002 transfer as A_ij^K A_kl^K=δ_(jk)(c_j in K) A_il^K and (D in K)Id_U=Σ_i(∏_(t≠i)(c_t in K))A_ii^K. All sums and products here are finite and σ preserves integer scalar multiples.

argument.text: N003 supplies (c_j in K)≠0 and (D in K)≠0. Define F_ij as stated. By F002, F_ijF_kl=δ_(jk)(c_l in K)^(-1)A_il^K=δ_(jk)F_il. Divide the diagonal identity of F002 by D. Since D=c_i∏_(t≠i)c_t and c_i and D have nonzero images, the coefficient D^(-1)∏_(t≠i)c_t equals c_i^(-1) in K. Thus Σ_iF_ii=Id_U. These calculations include λ=0, when all coefficients equal one.

argument.text: By D002 and D003, the identities r!X_r=x^r and r!Y_r=y^r hold as complex endomorphisms. Both sides preserve M by H003 and F001, and their coefficients r! are integers. Restrict to M and apply the homomorphism σ of F002 to obtain (r! in K)X_r^K=(x^K)^r and (r! in K)Y_r^K=(y^K)^r. In particular these hold for all r≤λ, as required. Combine these identities with F003 to conclude the required output, universally over the indices. The auxiliary choices ρ and τ occur only in the proof, since the resulting induced operators have the fixed D009 pure-tensor formula.

argument.text: H001 gives n=λ+1>0. H003 supplies an integer basis b of M indexed by some type I whose images in V are a complex basis. Regard that image family as a complex basis and apply M006 over C to V; its index cardinal Nat.card I is dim_C V=λ+1=n by H002. The index type is in fact finite: a basis of the finite-dimensional V has finitely many elements, since its linearly independent vectors cannot outnumber a finite spanning family. Thus its finite cardinal is n and it can be reindexed by Fin n. Reindexing the original integer basis by this bijection proves that M has an integer basis indexed by Fin n. The reindexing leaves M arbitrary and gives it no special form.

Use M007 to choose τ:U→K⊗_Z M. It is K-linear: for every pure tensor m0⊗a and scalar d, τ(d·(m0⊗a))=da⊗m0=d·τ(m0⊗a), and additivity extends this to all finite sums of pure tensors. Its inverse is also K-linear. Define Cbase_i=τ^(-1)(B_i)=m_i⊗1. Transporting linear relations and spanning expansions through τ shows that Cbase is a K-basis of U with index Fin n: a relation maps to the corresponding relation among B, and an expansion of τ(u) in B pulls back to an expansion of u in Cbase.

argument.text: Apply M006 over K to the basis Cbase of F003. It gives dim_K U=Nat.card(Fin n)=n=λ+1. This basis is finite, so U is finite-dimensional. As n>0, index 0 belongs to Fin n and Cbase_0 is nonzero by independence: if it were zero, the relation with coefficient 1 at 0 and zero elsewhere would contradict independence over the field K. Therefore U≠0. These are exactly the two clauses of the required output. The auxiliary basis and flip choices do not occur in the conclusion.

argument.text: The induced operator on a product of lattice-preserving maps equals the product of their induced operators. Indeed both sides send each pure tensor m0⊗a to the tensor of the composite applied to m0 with a, and equality extends to all tensors by linearity. The induced maps used here are supplied as such by N004 and D009, so their underlying restrictions preserve M. Consequently A_ij^K=X_(λ−i)^K Y_λ^K X_λ^K Y_(λ−j)^K. H001 gives 0≤λ−i,λ−j≤λ for all indices i,j≤λ. Each factor preserves W by F002, so their composite does. Its scalar multiple (c_j in K)^(-1)A_ij^K=F_ij also preserves W. N003 ensures the specified nonzero binomial normalization. The four-factor computation is valid even at λ=0, where the factors are identities.
